task.question: What institution produced data suggesting over 2,700 deaths due to heatwaves in the United Kingdom in 2026?
task.evidence: 2026 United Kingdom heatwaves: Data produced by Imperial College London, the Met Office and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine suggests that more than 2,700 deaths may have occurred as a result of the heatwaves in May and June.

Based on the article, the data suggesting over 2,700 deaths due to heatwaves in the United Kingdom in 2026 came from a collaborative study by **Imperial College London**, the **London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine**, and the **Met Office**. These three institutions jointly produced estimates showing approximately 550 deaths from the May heatwave and 2,200 deaths from the June heatwave, totaling roughly 2,700 deaths.

Additionally, the **UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA)** also produced estimates using a different methodology.

^ "May and June heatwaves killed about 2,700 people in England and Wales, data suggests" . The Guardian . 12 July 2026 . Retrieved 3 August 2026 .
Data from the Environment Agency show that in late July England's reservoirs were at 72% of capacity; three reservoirs were "exceptionally low" – Hanningfield in Essex (65% full), Blagdon in Somerset (56%), and Wimbleball in Somerset (54%) – and a further seven were "notably low". [ 141 ]
The second heatwave started on 19 June and saw more records broken, including that for hottest day during June when 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) was recorded in Lingwood , Norfolk on 26 June, which is also the fifth hottest day in the UK ever. The previous record for June of 35.6 °C (96.1 °F) was set in 1957 and 1976. A further 2,200 deaths were estimated to have occurred during this heatwave, bringing the total to roughly 2,700.
An estimate from Imperial College London , the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and the Met Office published in mid-July placed the number of deaths from the heat between 21 and 29 May at around 550. [ 1 ] An interim report on heat-associated deaths by the UK Health Security Agency using a different methodology estimated that there were 753 deaths linked to the May heatwave. [ 2 ] Between 24 and 31 May, at least 20 people died in water-related incidents across the country, including 14 children, prompting water safety experts to urge the government to treat drownings as a "public health disaster". [ 17 ]
The study by the Imperial College London, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and the Met Office estimated that 2,200 heat-related deaths took place between 18 and 28 June. [ 1 ] The UKHSA interim report estimated there were 2,124 heat-associated deaths in 21 to 28 June. [ 2 ] At least five people died in water-related incidents during the heatwave. On 24 June, a 50-year-old man died after entering the water at Aberavon Beach in south Wales. [ 48 ] On 26 June, the body of a 13-year-old boy was recovered from a lake in Syston after he was reported missing the previous day. [ 49 ] On 26 June, a 69-year-old man died after getting into difficulty in the water at Clacton-on-Sea . [ 50 ] On 27 June, the body of a 15-year-old boy last seen on 24 June was recovered from Testwood Lakes near Southampton , [ 51 ] whilst that of a 22-year-old man last seen in the early hours of the previous day was recovered from the River Severn in Shrewsbury .
